# AGENTS.md

Instructions for coding agents (Claude Code reads this via the `CLAUDE.md` symlink).

## Repository

Our buyer agent for the Tacto Negotiation Arena (EHL Final 2026).

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `agent/` | `negotiator`: arena API client, runner, telemetry, reports, strategies (Python 3.12, uv) |
| `negotiation-arena-kit/` | git submodule: brief, API docs, data package, starter kit (read-only, do not edit) |
| `bmw_data/` | Source data, git-ignored; never commit it or copy values from it into code |

## Commands

```sh
make install                                   # submodule + uv sync
make test && make lint                         # pytest (incl. arena-sim end to end), ruff
cd agent && uv run negotiator --help           # every API call, play/run/final, report, stats
```

Arena: the key is `ARENA_API_KEY` in the root `.env`. Practice is limited to 200 sessions a day - develop on
`--set sandbox` and the local `arena-sim`; never hard-code values from the data package or replays into code.
During the Live Final the agent must not read the live feed, leaderboard or results (`NEGOTIATOR_FINAL=1`
blocks them in the client).

Before a practice run, try a change to the numbers on `negotiator sim bench` (suppliers fitted from our replays,
no quota); it cannot judge wording, and a difference under 0.08 is noise - see `agent/docs/simulator.md`.

## Benchmarks

Every benchmark run (any `negotiator run` / `play` on sandbox or practice that is used to judge a strategy) gets a
record in `agent/docs/benchmarks/<date>-<strategy>-<model>.md` (e.g. `2026-10-10-lowball-none.md`; `none` when the
strategy uses no LLM), in the same change as the code it measures. Copy the layout of an existing record:

- **Result and cost first:** score per case and mean; the deal's cost `C_deal` in EUR; what the run cost us (practice
  sessions spent, LLM tokens, wall time).
- **Strategy:** its file, a one-line description, the parameters it ran with and the commit - so a later change to
  the strategy can be told apart from the old numbers.
- **Runs:** set and cases, run ID(s) under `agent/runs/`.

A repeat on the same day with the same parameters adds a row to that record; changed parameters or a new day get a
new file. Never rewrite old numbers. Add a line for the run to the overview in `agent/docs/benchmarks/README.md`.
A strategy without an LLM gets the same replies for the same e-mails, so one run is enough; with an LLM the text
varies - compare means over at least three repetitions. Start runs one at a time: the key allows 10 open sessions.

## HARD RULE: confirm before spending practice quota

Practice sessions are a scarce team budget: 200 per team per rolling 24 hours, shared by everyone on the team. A
coding agent must **never** start anything that spends quota without an explicit "yes" from a human in the
conversation, for that specific run. No exceptions, no assumed consent, no carrying a previous "yes" over to a new run.

**What spends quota:** every new practice session, which means:
- `negotiator play <case>` on a practice case (`case:P…`);
- `negotiator run --set practice`;
- `make` targets or scripts that call either of these;
- `POST /v1/sessions` for a practice case.

**What does not spend quota:** `--set sandbox` (cases `case:D…`), the local `arena-sim`, read-only calls
(`me`, `cases`, `sessions`, `session`, `thread`), and the final.

**Before asking, the agent must:**

1. Run `negotiator me` and read the current balance (`used`, `left`, `resets_at`).
2. Ask for confirmation, stating:
   - the exact command;
   - which cases it plays and how many sessions it will spend;
   - the balance before and after the run;
   - when the quota resets.
3. Wait for an explicit yes. Silence, "ok, continue with the task" or approval of an earlier run do not count. If
   the answer is anything but a clear yes, do not run it.

Example of the required question:

> This spends practice quota: `uv run negotiator run --set practice --cases case:P01 case:P05 --strategy tactical`
> → 2 sessions. Balance now 197 / 200 left, after the run 195. Quota resets at 2026-10-11 12:47 UTC. Run it?

## Run registry and pushed code only

**Never run unpushed code on a limited run.** A practice run, or any run that spends quota, must use code that is
committed **and pushed**. Before starting it:
- `git status` is clean;
- `git log origin/main..HEAD` is empty, or the branch is pushed;
- note the hash from `git rev-parse --short HEAD`.

Without this nobody can reproduce or compare the result, and the quota spent on it is wasted. Free runs (sandbox,
local `arena-sim`) may use uncommitted code.

**Every run goes into the registry** [`agent/docs/runs.md`](agent/docs/runs.md): practice runs always, sandbox runs
when they inform a decision. One row per run, with these columns:
- commit;
- strategy;
- parameters (cases, `--llm`, flags);
- author;
- description;
- results (per-case scores and the mean);
- conclusions.

Add the row in the same change that discusses the result.

# AGENTS.md

Instructions for coding agents (Claude Code reads this via the `CLAUDE.md` symlink).

## Repository

Our buyer agent for the Tacto Negotiation Arena (EHL Final 2026).

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `agent/` | `negotiator`: arena API client, runner, telemetry, reports, strategies (Python 3.12, uv) |
| `negotiation-arena-kit/` | git submodule: brief, API docs, data package, starter kit (read-only, do not edit) |
| `bmw_data/` | Source data, git-ignored; never commit it or copy values from it into code |

## Commands

```sh
make install                                   # submodule + uv sync
make test && make lint                         # pytest (incl. arena-sim end to end), ruff
cd agent && uv run negotiator --help           # every API call, play/run/final, report, stats
```

Arena: the key is `ARENA_API_KEY` in the root `.env`. Practice is limited to 200 sessions a day - develop on
`--set sandbox` and the local `arena-sim`; never hard-code values from the data package or replays into code.
During the Live Final the agent must not read the live feed, leaderboard or results (`NEGOTIATOR_FINAL=1`
blocks them in the client).

Before a practice run, try a change to the numbers on `negotiator sim bench` (suppliers fitted from our replays,
no quota); it cannot judge wording, and a difference under 0.08 is noise - see `agent/docs/simulator.md`.

## Benchmarks

Every benchmark run (any `negotiator run` / `play` on sandbox or practice that is used to judge a strategy) gets a
record in `agent/docs/benchmarks/<date>-<strategy>-<model>.md` (e.g. `2026-10-10-lowball-none.md`; `none` when the
strategy uses no LLM), in the same change as the code it measures. Copy the layout of an existing record:

- **Result and cost first:** score per case and mean; the deal's cost `C_deal` in EUR; what the run cost us (practice
  sessions spent, LLM tokens, wall time).
- **Strategy:** its file, a one-line description, the parameters it ran with and the commit - so a later change to
  the strategy can be told apart from the old numbers.
- **Runs:** set and cases, run ID(s) under `agent/runs/`.

A repeat on the same day with the same parameters adds a row to that record; changed parameters or a new day get a
new file. Never rewrite old numbers. Add a line for the run to the overview in `agent/docs/benchmarks/README.md`.
A strategy without an LLM gets the same replies for the same e-mails, so one run is enough; with an LLM the text
varies - compare means over at least three repetitions. Start runs one at a time: the key allows 10 open sessions.

## HARD RULE: confirm before spending practice quota

Practice sessions are a scarce team budget: 200 per team per rolling 24 hours, shared by everyone on the team. A
coding agent must **never** start anything that spends quota without an explicit "yes" from a human in the
conversation, for that specific run. No exceptions, no assumed consent, no carrying a previous "yes" over to a new run.

**What spends quota:** every new practice session, which means:
- `negotiator play <case>` on a practice case (`case:P…`);
- `negotiator run --set practice`;
- `make` targets or scripts that call either of these;
- `POST /v1/sessions` for a practice case.

**What does not spend quota:** `--set sandbox` (cases `case:D…`), the local `arena-sim`, read-only calls
(`me`, `cases`, `sessions`, `session`, `thread`), and the final.

**Before asking, the agent must:**

1. Run `negotiator me` and read the current balance (`used`, `left`, `resets_at`).
2. Ask for confirmation, stating:
   - the exact command;
   - which cases it plays and how many sessions it will spend;
   - the balance before and after the run;
   - when the quota resets.
3. Wait for an explicit yes. Silence, "ok, continue with the task" or approval of an earlier run do not count. If
   the answer is anything but a clear yes, do not run it.

Example of the required question:

> This spends practice quota: `uv run negotiator run --set practice --cases case:P01 case:P05 --strategy tactical`
> → 2 sessions. Balance now 197 / 200 left, after the run 195. Quota resets at 2026-10-11 12:47 UTC. Run it?

## Run registry and pushed code only

**Never run unpushed code on a limited run.** A practice run, or any run that spends quota, must use code that is
committed **and pushed**. Before starting it:
- `git status` is clean;
- `git log origin/main..HEAD` is empty, or the branch is pushed;
- note the hash from `git rev-parse --short HEAD`.

Without this nobody can reproduce or compare the result, and the quota spent on it is wasted. Free runs (sandbox,
local `arena-sim`) may use uncommitted code.

**Every run goes into the registry** [`agent/docs/runs.md`](agent/docs/runs.md): practice runs always, sandbox runs
when they inform a decision. One row per run, with these columns:
- commit;
- strategy;
- parameters (cases, `--llm`, flags);
- author;
- description;
- results (per-case scores and the mean);
- conclusions.

## Ideas tried

[`agent/docs/TRYED.md`](agent/docs/TRYED.md) lists every idea we have tried: what it was, where it was measured, and
the result - worked (and why), failed (and why), or unknown. Read it before proposing a change, so nobody tests the
same idea twice. Add or update a row in the same change that tries an idea: when the code for it lands (result
"unknown") and again when a run has settled it. Ideas that came from reading replays and were never played go in as
"unknown" too.

## Case triage: where to spend work and attempts

Before working on a strategy or asking for practice sessions, fill this table from the arena's live page
(`https://arena.tacto.ai/live`) and `negotiator me`. Five numbers per case: **ours** (our best score), **house**
(Tacto's house agent), **best** (the best team), **tried** (teams that played it), **beaten** (teams above the house).

Put each case in the first category that fits, and sort inside a category by the gap `best − ours`:

1. **Below the house.** A fault in our agent. First priority.
2. **Above the house, far from the best, and many of the teams that tried beat the house.** There is a known lever
   we do not use. Second priority.
3. **Close to the best, or a high house score that few teams beat.** A ceiling. Spend no attempts.

As of 11 October 2026: house, best, tried and beaten from the live page of 10 October at about 21:05; ours from
`negotiator me` on 11 October at 01:05. Rows keep the order of 10 October (P03 is above the house now). Refresh both before using it.

| Category | Case | Lever, goal | Ours | House | Best | Tried | Beaten | Gap to best |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | P08 | raw material, leverage | 0.626 | 0.75 | 0.91 | 22 | 1 | 0.284 |
| 1 | P02 | price increase, stabilise | 0.733 | 0.74 | 0.85 | 21 | 1 | 0.117 |
| 1 | P07 | bundling, routine | 0.740 | 0.78 | 0.81 | 21 | 1 | 0.070 |
| 1 | P01 | price increase, stabilise | 0.969 | 0.97 | 0.99 | 22 | 2 | 0.021 |
| 1 | P10 | capacity, secure_supply | 0.663 | 0.69 | 0.70 | 22 | 3 | 0.037 |
| 1 | P03 | renewal, stabilise | 0.923 | 0.92 | 0.94 | 21 | 1 | 0.017 |
| 2 | P11 | quality, quality_first | 0.692 | 0.31 | 0.81 | 20 | 17 | 0.118 |
| 2 | P05 | RFQ, leverage | 0.839 | 0.56 | 0.92 | 21 | 12 | 0.081 |
| 2 | P18 | raw material, leverage | 0.618 | 0.39 | 0.68 | 20 | 17 | 0.062 |
| 3 | P04 | renewal, routine | 0.860 | 0.86 | 0.87 | 21 | 14 | 0.010 |

We are below the house on six cases. Four of them are `stabilise` or `secure_supply` cases (see the next section).
P01, P02, P10 and P03 are in category 1 by the rule and within 0.12 of the best team.

## Firmness follows the case goal

How hard the agent pushes on price depends on the case's `category_goal`, not on the supplier's opening:

- **`leverage`** (raw material, RFQ): push. Only price and terms count in C.
- **`stabilise` and `secure_supply`:** do not push the price below what the supplier can live on. C carries a
  relationship charge for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below its sustainable margin
  (`RELATIONSHIP_GOALS` in `arena_kit/cost.py`), so a lower price can cost more than it saves.

Measured on P02 (`stabilise`), [`agent/docs/runs.md`](agent/docs/runs.md) P-13 and P-15:

| Deal price | Relationship charge | Score |
|---|---|---|
| EUR 358.45 | 56,127 | 0.686 |
| EUR 345.39 | 179,204 | 0.000 (C above C_open) |

Our cost estimate had the charge at 0 in both deals. Since `7143676` it is in our C (the supplier's standard terms
from its master data, its full cost at 0.98 of the own-plant should-cost), and the recorded charges are reproduced
to within EUR 56.

**The target is the price that minimises C with the charge, not the price where the charge starts.** Measured
([`agent/docs/investigation-2026-10-10.md`](agent/docs/investigation-2026-10-10.md), `runs.md` P-16 to P-22):

| Case | Price where the charge starts → score | Deal near the minimum of C → score |
|---|---|---|
| P01 | 138.41 at 14 days from April → 0.660 | 131.30 at 30 days from January → 0.969 |
| P02 | 373.56 at 90 days → 0.305 | 362.02 at 90 days with a 5 % deadband clause → 0.733 |

A strategy change that lowers prices must still be checked on the `stabilise` and `secure_supply` cases, and on a
case without a should-cost of the supplier's own plant the charge stays out of our C (sandbox D01).

## Rules

Read the file for the area you touch before changing it:

- [`.agents/git.md`](.agents/git.md) — commit messages (Conventional Commits), branches, pre-commit checks
- [`agent/README.md`](agent/README.md) — package architecture, telemetry layout, how to add a strategy
- [`agent/docs/benchmarks/`](agent/docs/benchmarks/) — one record per benchmark run (see Benchmarks above)
- [`agent/docs/knowledge/competitions-info.md`](agent/docs/knowledge/competitions-info.md) — scoring, practice and
  final rules from the arena's FAQ that the brief does not state; read it before changing how we score, close or run
- [`agent/docs/TRYED.md`](agent/docs/TRYED.md) — every idea tried and what came of it (see Ideas tried above)

## Case triage: where to spend work and attempts

Before working on a strategy or asking for practice sessions, fill this table from the arena's live page
(`https://arena.tacto.ai/live`) and `negotiator me`. Five numbers per case: **ours** (our best score), **house**
(Tacto's house agent), **best** (the best team), **tried** (teams that played it), **beaten** (teams above the house).

Put each case in the first category that fits, and sort inside a category by the gap `best − ours`:

1. **Below the house.** A fault in our agent. First priority.
2. **Above the house, far from the best, and many of the teams that tried beat the house.** There is a known lever
   we do not use. Second priority.
3. **Close to the best, or a high house score that few teams beat.** A ceiling. Spend no attempts.

## Firmness follows the case goal

How hard the agent pushes on price depends on the case's `category_goal`, not on the supplier's opening:

- **`leverage`** (raw material, RFQ): push. Only price and terms count in C.
- **`stabilise` and `secure_supply`:** do not push the price below what the supplier can live on. C carries a
  relationship charge for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below its sustainable margin
  (`RELATIONSHIP_GOALS` in `arena_kit/cost.py`), so a lower price can cost more than it saves.

Measured on P02 (`stabilise`), [`agent/docs/runs.md`](agent/docs/runs.md) P-13 and P-15:

| Deal price | Relationship charge | Score |
|---|---|---|
| EUR 358.45 | 56,127 | 0.686 |
| EUR 345.39 | 179,204 | 0.000 (C above C_open) |

Our cost estimate had the charge at 0 in both deals. Since `7143676` it is in our C (the supplier's standard terms
from its master data, its full cost at 0.98 of the own-plant should-cost), and the recorded charges are reproduced
to within EUR 56.

**The target is the price that minimises C with the charge, not the price where the charge starts.** Measured
([`agent/docs/investigation-2026-10-10.md`](agent/docs/investigation-2026-10-10.md), `runs.md` P-16 to P-22):

A strategy change that lowers prices must still be checked on the `stabilise` and `secure_supply` cases, and on a
case without a should-cost of the supplier's own plant the charge stays out of our C (sandbox D01).

# Git rules

## Commit messages: Conventional Commits

```
<type>(<scope>): <subject>

<body: why, not what — optional>

<footer: BREAKING CHANGE: ..., Refs: #123 — optional>
```

**Types**

| Type | Use for |
|---|---|
| `feat` | New user-facing behaviour |
| `fix` | Bug fix |
| `refactor` | Code change with no behaviour change |
| `perf` | Performance improvement |
| `test` | Adding or fixing tests only |
| `docs` | Documentation only (README, AGENTS.md, .agents/, comments) |
| `style` | Formatting only (ruff format, prettier); no logic |
| `build` | Dependencies, lockfiles, Makefile, the submodule pin |
| `ci` | CI pipelines |
| `chore` | Repo maintenance that fits nothing above (gitignore, tooling config) |
| `revert` | Reverting an earlier commit |

**Scopes** (optional, one per commit): `agent` (the negotiator package), `strategy` (negotiation logic in
`agent/src/negotiator/strategy/`), `kit` (the submodule pin), `repo` (root files). Omit the scope when a
change spans several areas.

**Subject**
- Imperative mood, lower case, no trailing period: `add item search endpoint`, not `Added item search.`
- At most 72 characters for the whole first line.
- Describe the effect, not the file: `fix(agent): retry a dropped reply with the same move id`.

**Body**: wrap at 72 characters; explain the reason and any trade-off. Required for `BREAKING CHANGE`
(also mark the type with `!`: `feat(agent)!: rename the run command to play-set`).

**One logical change per commit.** Formatting-only changes go in their own `style` commit. A strategy
change and the tests that pin its behaviour go in the same commit.

Examples:
```
feat(strategy): ask for a cost breakdown before the second offer
fix(agent): keep held RFQ threads alive while others negotiate
build(kit): update negotiation-arena-kit to the Sunday release
test(agent): cover the final-mode guard
docs: describe commit rules in .agents/git.md
```

## Branches

`<type>/<short-kebab-description>` from `main`, e.g. `feat/llm-strategy`, `fix/keepalive-timing`.
Keep `main` deployable; merge through pull requests, squash when the branch history is noisy.

## Before committing

- `make test && make lint` (ruff and pytest in `agent/`).
- Never commit secrets (`.env`, API keys), data (`bmw_data/`, `agent/data/`), run telemetry (`agent/runs/`),
  virtualenvs or caches.
- Commit, pull and push regularly without being asked (see AGENTS.md, Rules); never push to `main` directly and
  never force-push it.

# Git rules

## Commit messages: Conventional Commits

```
<type>(<scope>): <subject>

<body: why, not what — optional>

<footer: BREAKING CHANGE: ..., Refs: #123 — optional>
```

**Types**

| Type | Use for |
|---|---|
| `feat` | New user-facing behaviour |
| `fix` | Bug fix |
| `refactor` | Code change with no behaviour change |
| `perf` | Performance improvement |
| `test` | Adding or fixing tests only |
| `docs` | Documentation only (README, AGENTS.md, .agents/, comments) |
| `style` | Formatting only (ruff format, prettier); no logic |
| `build` | Dependencies, lockfiles, Makefile, the submodule pin |
| `ci` | CI pipelines |
| `chore` | Repo maintenance that fits nothing above (gitignore, tooling config) |
| `revert` | Reverting an earlier commit |

**Scopes** (optional, one per commit): `agent` (the negotiator package), `strategy` (negotiation logic in
`agent/src/negotiator/strategy/`), `kit` (the submodule pin), `repo` (root files). Omit the scope when a
change spans several areas.

**Subject**
- Imperative mood, lower case, no trailing period: `add item search endpoint`, not `Added item search.`
- At most 72 characters for the whole first line.
- Describe the effect, not the file: `fix(agent): retry a dropped reply with the same move id`.

**Body**: wrap at 72 characters; explain the reason and any trade-off. Required for `BREAKING CHANGE`
(also mark the type with `!`: `feat(agent)!: rename the run command to play-set`).

**One logical change per commit.** Formatting-only changes go in their own `style` commit. A strategy
change and the tests that pin its behaviour go in the same commit.

Examples:
```
feat(strategy): ask for a cost breakdown before the second offer
fix(agent): keep held RFQ threads alive while others negotiate
build(kit): update negotiation-arena-kit to the Sunday release
test(agent): cover the final-mode guard
docs: describe commit rules in .agents/git.md
```

## Branches

`<type>/<short-kebab-description>` from `main`, e.g. `feat/llm-strategy`, `fix/keepalive-timing`.
Keep `main` deployable; merge through pull requests, squash when the branch history is noisy.

## Before committing

- `make test && make lint` (ruff and pytest in `agent/`).
- Never commit secrets (`.env`, API keys), data (`bmw_data/`, `agent/data/`), run telemetry (`agent/runs/`),
  virtualenvs or caches.
- Commit, pull and push regularly without being asked (see AGENTS.md, Rules); never push to `main` directly and
  never force-push it.

1	"""Tactical buyer: category goal + supplier profile -> tactics; tit-for-tat Boulware concessions in C.
2	
3	Ideas taken from ASTRA (Kwon et al., github.com/DSincerity/ASTRA-NegoAgent) - the tactics, not the
4	code: a model of the opponent, an optimiser over the published cost function, several offers of
5	equal value to us that differ in what they give the supplier, and concessions that answer the
6	supplier's (no move from it, no move from us).
7	
8	Per case (prepare):
9	  - the category goal sets the policy: how deep we anchor, how slowly we concede (Boulware beta),
10	    how much of the supplier's move we answer (reciprocity), whether we protect its margin;
11	  - the supplier's profile (profile.py) adjusts it: idle capacity -> anchor deeper; fully booked or
12	    below cost -> shallower; cash-short -> offer early payment; hedged -> skip index arguments ...;
13	  - target C: the deepest credible price (anchor, should-cost, history, alternative), never below
14	    what the supplier can sell at (its full cost, plus the sustainable margin where squeezing costs C).
15	
16	Per round (decide), all in C (our total cost, the score's currency):
17	  - their concession = drop of C of their standing sheet; ours = drop of the C we ask for;
18	  - next ask: the Boulware curve over the rounds we can still play (round limit and the clock),
19	    capped by reciprocity - if they did not move, we hold (then a half step to break a deadlock;
20	    the third stall settles the thread);
21	  - up to three term sheets at that same C: our C-optimal terms; a trade the supplier values
22	    (early payment for the cash-short, a long commitment for those who want volume or security);
23	    a pure price move on its own terms. Whatever it agrees to costs us the same.
24	  - arguments: checkable evidence picked by the profile; what came back irrelevant or contradicted
25	    is not used again.
26	Closing: the cheapest standing sheet that passes the guards (guards.py), else walk away; a
27	`final_offer` is probed once with a trade when walking would cost us little. Our estimate of its floor
28	never ends an open thread: the supplier does (a final offer, firm words, a stall) or the rounds run out.
29	Conduct (conduct.py): honest, sourced, no empty threats, the supplier's margin respected - code-checked on send.

244	        unknown = set(flags) - set(FLAGS)
245	        if unknown:
246	            raise ValueError(f"unknown tactical flags: {sorted(unknown)}")
247	        self.flags = {name: bool(flags.get(name, False)) for name in FLAGS}

252	    def prepare(self, neg: Negotiation) -> None:
253	        if neg.data is not None:
254	            self.data = neg.data  # the session's view for this case: its own facts (WorldData.with_case)
255	        buyer = neg.buyer
256	        goal = buyer.get("category_goal", "routine")
257	        parts = neg.case.get("parts") or []
258	        current = buyer.get("current_unit_price")
259	        for sid, thread in neg.threads.items():
260	            _, terms = thread.standing
261	            profile = build_profile(self.data, sid, neg.case)
262	            policy = self._policy(goal, profile)
263	            full_cost = self._full_cost(parts, sid)
264	            cost_source = "own plant" if full_cost else ""
265	            if full_cost and goal in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
266	                full_cost = round(full_cost * SHOULD_COST_SHARE, 2)  # one cost for the charge and the floor
267	            guess = None
268	            if not full_cost and goal in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
269	                guessed, cost_source = self._fallback_full_cost(neg, sid)
270	                guess = self._supplier_estimate(neg, sid, guessed, profile) if guessed else None
271	            self._estimate_supplier(neg, sid, full_cost, profile)
272	            floor = self._floor(neg, full_cost, policy)
273	            open_c = neg.cost(sid, terms)
274	            gt = estimate(self.data, neg.case, sid, terms.get("unit_price"), tuple(profile.traits))
275	            if gt.lower and goal not in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
276	                floor = gt.lower  # one floor: the ground truth's (it knows below-cost sellers and countries)
277	            target_c = self._target_c(neg, sid, terms, policy, profile, floor, current, gt)
278	            plan = Plan(sid, self._name(sid), policy, profile, open_c, target_c, floor, full_cost, gt)
279	            plan.guess = guess
280	            plan.lower_c, plan.upper_c = self._bounds_c(neg, sid, terms, gt, target_c, open_c)
281	            if terms.get("unit_price") is not None:
282	                rate = buyer.get("interest_rate", 0.08) * (2 if profile.has("cash_short") else 1)
283	                plan.belief = FloorBelief(neg.case, terms, thread.standard_terms, gt.lower, rate)
284	                plan.belief.ppm = profile.ppm  # scorecard ppm: what a chargeback really costs it
285	            plan.evidence = self._evidence(neg, sid, terms.get("unit_price"), current) if terms else []
286	            if self.flags["news"] and terms:
287	                plan.evidence += self._news_evidence(neg, sid, profile)
288	            body = thread.latest.get("body") or ""
289	            clauses = [o for o in neg.case.get("term_options", {}).get("index_clause") or [] if o]
290	            if "index_clause" in neg.case["negotiable"] and any(o.get("series") in body for o in clauses):
291	                # it argues its price with the very index a clause would follow: the clause answers it. P02's
292	                # supplier dropped its price by 15-22 for one and never went under 372.96 without (P-13, P-15, P-19)
293	                plan.requests.add("index_clause")
294	            if profile.has("hedged"):
295	                plan.banned_kinds.add("index")  # "not our reality" until its hedge runs out
296	            if gt.market_supports_ask:
297	                plan.banned_kinds.add("index")  # the indices back its ask: citing them helps it, not us
298	            self.tplans[sid] = plan
299	            neg.recorder.event(
300	                "plan",
301	                session_id=neg.session_id,

308	                trait_refs=profile.traits,

311	                target_c=target_c,
312	                lower_c=plan.lower_c,

322	            log.info(

324	                sid,
325	                goal,
326	                ",".join(sorted(profile.traits)) or "-",
327	                terms.get("unit_price"),
328	                gt.lower,

336	    def _policy(self, goal: str, p: SupplierProfile) -> Policy:
337	        base = POLICIES.get(goal, DEFAULT_POLICY)
338	        anchor, beta, recip = base.anchor, base.beta, base.reciprocity
339	        trade = list(base.trade_first)
340	        if p.has("underutilised"):
341	            anchor, beta = anchor + 0.03, beta + 0.5
342	        markup = base.markup
343	        if p.has("full_order_book") or p.has("below_cost"):
344	            anchor = max(0.02, anchor - 0.03)
345	            markup = max(markup, 0.0)  # no room under its cost: it is already there or does not need us
346	        if p.has("price_frozen"):
347	            anchor = max(0.02, anchor - 0.02)
348	        if p.has("approval_ladder"):
349	            beta += 0.5  # it moves in small approved steps: no reason for us to move fast
350	        if p.has("cash_short"):
351	            trade.insert(0, "payment_days")
352	        if p.has("wants_volume") or p.has("full_order_book") or p.has("price_frozen"):
353	            trade += ["contract_months", "volume_per_year"]
354	        if p.has("we_pay_late") or p.has("relationship"):
355	            recip = min(1.0, recip + 0.1)
356	        return Policy(anchor, beta, recip, markup, base.claims_first, tuple(dict.fromkeys(trade)))
357	
358	    def _evidence(self, neg, sid, open_price, current):
359	        out = super()._evidence(neg, sid, open_price, current)
360	        if self.data:
361	            parts = neg.case.get("parts") or []
362	            out += self.data.evidence_orders(parts, sid, open_price)
363	            if self.flags["fresh_args"]:
364	                out += self.data.evidence_orders_per_part(parts, sid)
365	            out += data_facts(self.data, parts, all_windows=self.flags["all_windows"])
366	            if self.flags["fresh_claims"]:
367	                later = self.data.evidence_complaints(parts, sid, since="2025-10-01")
368	                if open_price and not any(e.kind == "should_cost" for e in out):
369	                    later += self.data.evidence_should_cost(parts, open_price, margin=1.0)
370	                for e in later:  # material for rounds 2+: round 1 already carries our best three
371	                    e.meta = {**(e.meta or {}), "later": True}
372	                out += later
373	        return sorted(out, key=lambda e: -e.strength)

375	    def _full_cost(self, parts: list[str], supplier_id: str) -> float | None:
376	        """The should-cost of THIS supplier's plant for a single-part case; None otherwise.
377	
378	        Another supplier's estimate is a different plant (cost base, process) and a bundle's price is
379	        not one part's cost: guessing would push the floor and the margin charge the wrong way."""
380	        if not self.data or len(parts) != 1:
381	            return None
382	        rows = self.data.query(
383	            "SELECT unit_cost FROM should_cost WHERE part_id = ? AND supplier_id = ? ORDER BY estimate_date DESC",
384	            (parts[0], supplier_id),
385	        )
386	        return rows[0]["unit_cost"] if rows and rows[0]["unit_cost"] else None
387	
388	    def _fallback_full_cost(self, neg: Negotiation, sid: str) -> tuple[float | None, str]:
389	        """A strategic supplier's full cost where its own plant has no should-cost: the price of the main sheet of
390	        its first message less the sustainable margin, x SHOULD_COST_SHARE (its alternatives are other structures,
391	        and a cheaper one would set the guess too low). None where the case puts no price on the supplier's margin
392	        (no charge to protect) or nothing is quoted."""
393	        buyer = neg.buyer
394	        margin = buyer.get("sustainable_margin_pct")
395	        if not margin or not buyer.get("relationship_eur_per_point"):
396	            return None, ""
397	        first = next((m for m in neg.threads[sid].supplier_messages if m.get("term_sheets")), None)
398	        opening = ((first or {}).get("term_sheets") or [{}])[0].get("terms", {}).get("unit_price")
399	        if not isinstance(opening, int | float) or opening <= 0:
400	            return None, ""
401	        return round(opening * (1 - margin / 100) * SHOULD_COST_SHARE, 2), "opening less the sustainable margin"
402	
403	    def _guess_floor(self, neg: Negotiation, sid: str, plan: Plan, terms: dict) -> float:
404	        """Under a guessed cost, the price that minimises C on these terms with the guessed charge (0 without a
405	        guess): no ask and no accept goes under it."""
406	        if not plan.guess or terms.get("unit_price") is None:
407	            return 0.0
408	        std = neg.threads[sid].standard_terms
409	
410	        def c(price: float) -> float:
411	            return total_cost(neg.case, {**terms, "unit_price": price}, std, plan.guess)
412	
413	        lo, hi = 0.0, terms["unit_price"] * 1.5
414	        for _ in range(60):
415	            a, b = lo + (hi - lo) / 3, hi - (hi - lo) / 3
416	            if c(a) < c(b):
417	                hi = b
418	            else:
419	                lo = a
420	        return math.ceil((lo + hi) / 2 * 100 - 1e-6) / 100
421	
422	    def _standard_terms(self, neg: Negotiation, sid: str) -> dict:
423	        """The supplier's standard terms for the relationship term: its quote PDF, then its master data, then its
424	        opening sheet. The PDFs of P01, P02, P03 and P10 name neither payment nor Incoterm, which left the charge
425	        out of C altogether (P02 closed at 345.39 with EUR 179k of it, score 0). What stays unknown is taken as
426	        the value that charges most - too high a charge costs a little price, too low a charge scores 0."""
427	        std = dict(neg.threads[sid].standard_terms)
428	        master = (self.data.supplier(sid) if self.data else None) or {}
429	        first = next((m for m in neg.threads[sid].supplier_messages if m.get("term_sheets")), None)
430	        opening = first["term_sheets"][0]["terms"] if first else {}
431	        fixed = neg.case.get("fixed_terms", {})
432	        for name in ("payment_days", "incoterm"):
433	            for source in (master, opening):
434	                if std.get(name) is None and fixed.get(name) is None and source.get(name) is not None:
435	                    std[name] = source[name]
436	        freight = neg.buyer["freight_eur_per_unit"]
437	        if std.get("incoterm") not in freight and fixed.get("incoterm") is None:
438	            std["incoterm"] = max(freight, key=freight.get)
439	        if std.get("payment_days") is None and fixed.get("payment_days") is None:
440	            options = neg.case.get("term_options", {}).get("payment_days") or []
441	            std["payment_days"] = min(options, default=neg.buyer["reference_payment_days"])
442	        return std

444	    def _estimate_supplier(self, neg: Negotiation, sid: str, full_cost: float | None, p: SupplierProfile) -> None:
445	        """Our estimate of the supplier for the relationship term in C (stabilise, secure_supply)."""
446	        if neg.buyer.get("category_goal") not in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS or not full_cost:
447	            neg.supplier_estimates.pop(sid, None)
448	            return
449	        neg.supplier_estimates[sid] = self._supplier_estimate(neg, sid, full_cost, p)

451	    def _supplier_estimate(self, neg: Negotiation, sid: str, full_cost: float, p: SupplierProfile) -> dict:
452	        rate = neg.buyer.get("interest_rate", 0.08)
453	        return {
454	            "full_cost": full_cost,
455	            "interest_rate": rate * CASH_SHORT_RATE if p.has("cash_short") else rate,  # money now is dearer to it
456	            "usual_rate": rate,
457	            "standard": self._standard_terms(neg, sid),
458	        }

460	    def _update_upper(self, neg: Negotiation, sid: str, plan: Plan) -> None:
461	        """The upper bound follows the evidence: where this supplier will stop with us (its offers, last words,
462	        the shrinking path of its steps), priced on the best structure. Offline on 28 practice sessions this
463	        estimate met the real stopping point within 8 % before the first reply and 1-3 % by round 3-4.
464	        The anchor stays where the data put it; only how far we go and when we take it follow the supplier."""
465	        _, theirs = neg.threads[sid].standing
466	        insisted = {r for r, n in plan.request_counts.items() if n >= 2}
467	        stop_c, stop_terms = plan.belief.best_package(
468	            lambda t: neg.cost(sid, t),
469	            lambda t: neg.keeps_must_haves(sid, t),
470	            allow=lambda t: all(satisfies(neg.case, t, theirs or {}, r, plan.proposed) for r in insisted),
471	        )
472	        if not math.isfinite(stop_c):
473	            return
474	        _, terms = neg.threads[sid].standing
475	        cap = min(neg.c_alt, neg.cost(sid, terms) if terms else math.inf, plan.open_c)
476	        before = plan.upper_c
477	        plan.stop_c = stop_c
478	        plan.upper_c = min(max(stop_c * (1 + STOP_MARGIN), plan.target_c * (1 + UPPER_ROOM)), cap)
479	        if neg.supplier_estimates.get(sid):
480	            # where only the price moves, 1 % and 6 % of C are more than the whole room (P01: 5 %, P02: 2 %):
481	            # the bound became the supplier's current offer and every offer counted as good enough - P01 took an
482	            # alternative in round 3 at 134.80 while the supplier was still coming down (0.733, P-20)
483	            room = max(0.0, plan.open_c - plan.target_c)
484	            plan.upper_c = min(max(stop_c + STOP_ROOM * room, plan.target_c + UPPER_ROOM_SHARE * room), cap)
485	        neg.recorder.event(
486	            "belief",
487	            session_id=neg.session_id,
488	            supplier_id=sid,
489	            belief=plan.belief.summary(),
490	            stop_c=round(stop_c, 2),
491	            stop_price=(stop_terms or {}).get("unit_price"),
492	            upper_before=round(before, 2) if math.isfinite(before) else None,
493	            upper_after=round(plan.upper_c, 2) if math.isfinite(plan.upper_c) else None,
494	        )
495	        log.info(
496	            "%s belief: stop ~%s (price %s), upper %s -> %s",
497	            sid,
498	            _k(stop_c),
499	            (stop_terms or {}).get("unit_price"),
500	            _k(before),
501	            _k(plan.upper_c),
502	        )

504	    def _floor(self, neg: Negotiation, full_cost: float | None, policy: Policy) -> float | None:
505	        if not full_cost:
506	            return None
507	        if neg.buyer.get("category_goal") in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
508	            margin = neg.buyer.get("sustainable_margin_pct") or 0
509	            return round(full_cost / (1 - margin / 100), 2)
510	        return round(full_cost * (1 + policy.markup), 2)
511	
512	    def _target_c(self, neg, sid, terms, policy, profile, floor, current, gt: GroundTruth | None = None) -> float:
513	        """The C of our first ask: the deepest credible price on our C-optimal terms - just under the
514	        supplier's estimated floor when we have one, else an anchor below the reference price."""
515	        open_price = terms.get("unit_price")
516	        if open_price is None:
517	            return math.inf
518	        price_only = bool(gt and gt.lower and gt.lower >= open_price * 0.95)  # the prior says: only the price moves
519	        depth = ANCHOR_PRICE_ONLY if price_only else ANCHOR_WITH_LEVERS
520	        extra = ANCHOR_DATA_EXTRA
521	        if neg.buyer.get("category_goal") == "routine":
522	            # P07 (bundling, routine): a 13 % ask got 5.59 and four rounds (0.721, P-13); 25-26 % got "your
523	            # target prices are not feasible", 5.69 and a final offer in round 2 (0.585 P-15, 0.663 P-22)
524	            depth, extra = min(depth, ANCHOR_ROUTINE), 0.0
525	        if neg.supplier_estimates.get(sid):
526	            # the margin charge is in C: the ask may go as deep as a price-only talk, it stops at the price that
527	            # costs us least (below). P01 came down to 132.20 after a 10 % ask, to 137.00 after a 3 % one
528	            depth, extra = ANCHOR_PRICE_ONLY, 0.0
529	        elif neg.buyer.get("category_goal") in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
530	            depth, extra = min(depth, ANCHOR_RELATIONSHIP), 0.0  # squeezing a strategic supplier costs us C
531	        # round 1 carries 67 % of all supplier movement and no supplier ever walked over a deep first offer
532	        # (0 of 917 replies); within a case deeper first offers went with better scores - so we open deep
533	        candidates = [open_price * (1 - depth)]
534	        if gt and gt.lower and gt.grounded:
535	            candidates.append(gt.lower * (1 - UNDER_FLOOR))
536	        alt_price = ((neg.buyer.get("alternative") or {}).get("terms") or {}).get("unit_price")
537	        if alt_price and alt_price < open_price:
538	            candidates.append(alt_price * 0.98)
539	        # the data may take it deeper - a cheaper alternative, a low grounded floor - but not past 5 points more
540	        price = max(min(candidates), open_price * (1 - depth - extra))
541	        # no hard floor for strategic suppliers: the relationship term already prices a squeeze in C, and
542	        # our cost estimate can sit above its real one (P02: should-cost 380 over a 371 quote, C_best ~364)
543	        price = min(price, open_price)
544	        ideal = complete_offer(neg.case, self._optimise(neg, sid, {**terms, "unit_price": round(price, 2)}))
545	        if neg.supplier_estimates.get(sid):
546	            # with the margin charge in C, a price under the one that costs us least costs more charge than it
547	            # saves - and the supplier may agree to it (P02 agreed to 345.39): the first ask stops there
548	            for _ in range(2):
549	                ideal["unit_price"] = max(ideal["unit_price"], round(self._cheapest_price(neg, sid, ideal), 2))
550	                ideal = complete_offer(neg.case, self._optimise(neg, sid, ideal))
551	        return min(neg.cost(sid, ideal), neg.cost(sid, terms))
552	
553	    def _bounds_c(self, neg, sid, terms, gt: GroundTruth, target_c: float, open_c: float) -> tuple[float, float]:
554	        """The bounds in C, on our C-optimal terms: a fair price on poor terms (a short contract that
555	        leaves need uncovered, early payment, dear freight) must not pass as a good deal."""
556	        lower_c, upper_c = -math.inf, min(open_c, neg.c_alt)
557	        if gt.lower:
558	            low = self._ideal(neg, sid, terms, gt.lower)
559	            if neg.supplier_estimates.get(sid):
560	                # under a margin charge a price below the one that costs us least costs more, not less: the bound
561	                # sits at that price (a floor factor of 0.86 under a strategic supplier's cost put it above its quote)
562	                low["unit_price"] = max(low["unit_price"], round(self._cheapest_price(neg, sid, low), 2))
563	            lower_c = neg.cost(sid, low)
564	        if gt.upper:
565	            upper_c = min(upper_c, neg.cost(sid, self._ideal(neg, sid, terms, gt.upper)))
566	        # room to concede above our first ask, whatever the calibration says (P05: an 18 % anchor over a 22 %
567	        # floor left upper == anchor and only 0.4 % steps) - never above its quote or our alternative
568	        return lower_c, min(max(upper_c, target_c * (1 + UPPER_ROOM)), open_c, neg.c_alt)
569	
570	    def _ideal(self, neg, sid, terms: dict, price: float) -> dict:
571	        return complete_offer(neg.case, self._optimise(neg, sid, {**terms, "unit_price": round(price, 2)}))
572	
573	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ per thread
574	    def decide(self, neg: Negotiation, supplier_id: str) -> Decision:
575	        t, plan = neg.threads[supplier_id], self.tplans[supplier_id]
576	        if not t.live:
577	            return Decision.drop(supplier_id, f"thread {t.status}")
578	        self._learn(neg, supplier_id, plan)
579	        sheet_id, theirs = neg.best_offer(supplier_id)  # judge it by its best sheet for us, not its first
580	        if theirs.get("unit_price") is None or not math.isfinite(plan.target_c):
581	            return Decision.hold(supplier_id, "no price to negotiate on")
582	        if text := self._text_price_offer(neg, supplier_id, plan):
583	            return text  # it wrote a lower price than it sheeted: ask for that first, even next to an agreement
584	        if t.status == "agreed":
585	            if take := self._take_agreed(neg, supplier_id):
586	                return take
587	            return Decision.hold(supplier_id, "agreed")
588	        limit = neg.case.get("round_limit") or 10
589	        if limit - t.arena_rounds <= 0 or (limit - t.rounds_used == 1 and t.our_price_path()):
590	            # the last round is kept for the close - unless we have not asked anything yet: with round_limit 1
591	            # holding would never send an offer at all
592	            return Decision.hold(supplier_id, "last round: keep it for the close")
593	        if neg.seconds_to_deadline() < 120:
594	            return Decision.hold(supplier_id, "the deadline is near")
595	        if counter := self._floor_counter(neg, supplier_id, plan, theirs):
596	            return counter
597	
598	        their_c = neg.cost(supplier_id, theirs)
599	        signals = reply_signals(t.latest.get("body", ""))
600	        # the lower bound is where we anchor, not where we stop: below it we keep asking - the supplier
601	        # ends it with a stall or a final offer, and only it knows its real floor
602	        closing_word = t.status == "final_offer" or (signals["firm"] and t.rounds_used > 0)
603	        rest_pending = self._rest_pending(neg, supplier_id, plan)
604	        if (
605	            not closing_word
606	            and not rest_pending
607	            and (their_c <= plan.lower_c or self._undercut_after_big_step(neg, supplier_id, plan, theirs))
608	        ):
609	            if reanchor := self._reanchor(neg, supplier_id, plan, theirs, their_c):
610	                return reanchor
611	        if alt := self._take_alternative(neg, supplier_id, plan):
612	            return alt  # its cheapest sheet is an alternative: the arena closes on the primary one, so ask for it
613	        last_word = t.status == "final_offer" or (signals["firm"] and t.rounds_used > 0)
614	        if last_word:
615	            # a last word is taken (the guards still check it): across ~65 pushes on final offers, 17 % ended in a
616	            # walk-away for ~+0.05 on average - only an RFQ with a safe rival offer may push once, with a real step
617	            if (
618	                their_c > plan.upper_c
619	                and not plan.probed_final
620	                and self._may_probe(neg, supplier_id, their_c)

773	    def _next_c(self, neg: Negotiation, sid: str, plan: Plan, their_c: float) -> float:
774	        """Boulware over the rounds we can still play, capped by what the supplier gave last."""
775	        if not plan.our_c:

777	        t = neg.threads[sid]
778	        last = plan.our_c[-1]
779	        budget = self._round_budget(neg, sid)
780	        progress = min(1.0, t.rounds_used / max(1, budget - 1))
781	        curve = plan.target_c + (their_c - plan.target_c) * progress**plan.policy.beta
782	        by_time = max(0.0, curve - last)
783	        theirs_path = self._their_c_path(neg, sid)
784	        their_move = theirs_path[-2] - theirs_path[-1] if len(theirs_path) >= 2 else 0.0
785	        min_step = MIN_STEP * last
786	        gap = max(0.0, their_c - last)

"""Tactical buyer: category goal + supplier profile -> tactics; tit-for-tat Boulware concessions in C.

Ideas taken from ASTRA (Kwon et al., github.com/DSincerity/ASTRA-NegoAgent) - the tactics, not the
code: a model of the opponent, an optimiser over the published cost function, several offers of
equal value to us that differ in what they give the supplier, and concessions that answer the
supplier's (no move from it, no move from us).

Per case (prepare):
  - the category goal sets the policy: how deep we anchor, how slowly we concede (Boulware beta),
    how much of the supplier's move we answer (reciprocity), whether we protect its margin;
  - the supplier's profile (profile.py) adjusts it: idle capacity -> anchor deeper; fully booked or
    below cost -> shallower; cash-short -> offer early payment; hedged -> skip index arguments ...;
  - target C: the deepest credible price (anchor, should-cost, history, alternative), never below
    what the supplier can sell at (its full cost, plus the sustainable margin where squeezing costs C).

Per round (decide), all in C (our total cost, the score's currency):
  - their concession = drop of C of their standing sheet; ours = drop of the C we ask for;
  - next ask: the Boulware curve over the rounds we can still play (round limit and the clock),
    capped by reciprocity - if they did not move, we hold (then a half step to break a deadlock;
    the third stall settles the thread);
  - up to three term sheets at that same C: our C-optimal terms; a trade the supplier values
    (early payment for the cash-short, a long commitment for those who want volume or security);
    a pure price move on its own terms. Whatever it agrees to costs us the same.
  - arguments: checkable evidence picked by the profile; what came back irrelevant or contradicted
    is not used again.
Closing: the cheapest standing sheet that passes the guards (guards.py), else walk away; a
`final_offer` is probed once with a trade when walking would cost us little. Our estimate of its floor
never ends an open thread: the supplier does (a final offer, firm words, a stall) or the rounds run out.
Conduct (conduct.py): honest, sourced, no empty threats, the supplier's margin respected - code-checked on send.
"""

import math
import re

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Policy:
    anchor: float  # first ask: this share below the reference price
    beta: float  # Boulware exponent: > 1 concedes late
    reciprocity: float  # share of the supplier's last concession (in C) we answer at most
    markup: float  # floor vs the supplier's full cost when its margin does not cost us C (suppliers have
    # sold below full cost to keep volume: a leverage floor may sit a little under it)
    claims_first: int = 3  # arguments in the first e-mail
    trade_first: tuple[str, ...] = ()  # levers to offer the supplier, in order


POLICIES = {
    "leverage": Policy(anchor=0.10, beta=3.0, reciprocity=0.6, markup=-0.03),
    "routine": Policy(anchor=0.07, beta=2.0, reciprocity=0.8, markup=0.0),
    "quality_first": Policy(anchor=0.05, beta=2.5, reciprocity=0.8, markup=0.0, trade_first=("contract_months",)),
    "stabilise": Policy(
        anchor=0.04, beta=2.0, reciprocity=1.0, markup=0.0, trade_first=("contract_months", "volume_per_year")
    ),
    "secure_supply": Policy(
        anchor=0.03, beta=1.8, reciprocity=1.0, markup=0.0, trade_first=("contract_months", "volume_per_year")
    ),
}
DEFAULT_POLICY = POLICIES["routine"]
STALL_EPS = 0.0005  # a C move below 0.05 % is no move
DONE_EPS = 0.001  # our ask within 0.1 % of their C: nothing left worth a round
ANCHOR_WITH_LEVERS = 0.25  # first ask 25 % under the quote where competition, material or capacity give a lever
ANCHOR_DATA_EXTRA = 0.05  # how much deeper the data may take the first ask
# The supplier's full cost as a share of its own plant's should-cost. The margin charges the arena recorded on
# P01, P02 and P03 (14 deals up to runs.md P-15) put it at 0.975-0.980; company.md gives the estimate an error of
# about 5 %. Too high a cost only leaves price on the table, too low a cost scores 0 - so the upper end.
SHOULD_COST_SHARE = 0.98
# What money now is worth to a supplier short of cash, as a multiple of our rate: P01's charges at 14, 45 and
# 60 days (runs.md P-2 to P-15) fit 9.6 % a year against our 8 %.
CASH_SHORT_RATE = 1.2
# Without its own plant's should-cost (the package has one for 18 suppliers) a strategic supplier's cost is
# guessed: its opening price less the sustainable margin, x SHOULD_COST_SHARE. Against the full cost the arena's
# recorded charges imply it sat +1.3 % (P01), -1.4 % (P02), +0.3 % (P03) and +3.5 % (D01) off. The guess is a floor
# only - no ask and no accept under the price that costs us least with the guessed charge - so nothing goes the way
# of P02 (EUR 345.39 against a should-cost of 380: charge EUR 179k, score 0); prices and concessions otherwise
# follow C without it, as an error of a few per cent in a charge inside C moved D01 from 0.749 to 0.627 (S-26).
RELATIONSHIP_COST_FLOOR = 0.95  # never ask a strategic supplier below 95 % of its should-cost
ANCHOR_RELATIONSHIP = 0.04  # stabilise / secure_supply: below its margin the deal costs us
ANCHOR_ROUTINE = 0.13  # routine goal: a deeper first ask is answered with a final offer
ANCHOR_PRICE_ONLY = 0.10  # ... and 10 % where only the price of a running relationship is at stake
MAX_ANCHOR = 0.15  # (kept for the experiments that import it)
MAX_ANCHOR_LEVERAGE = 0.18  # ... 18 % in leverage: floors sat 19-31 % under (D02, P05, P18), but a deeper first
# ask lost credibility (P05: Hrvelec walked after four rounds at 24-25 against its 34)
# without a cost estimate, anchor this far under the reference price (baseline v2's sandbox-tested depths)
GUESS_ANCHOR = {"leverage": 0.18, "routine": 0.12, "quality_first": 0.10, "stabilise": 0.06, "secure_supply": 0.05}
UNDER_FLOOR = 0.02  # the first ask sits this far under the supplier's estimated floor
ALT_ROOM_SHARE = 0.001  # its alternative must save this share of the room ...
ALT_MIN_EUR = 10.0  # ... and at least this much: below it a rounding of the sheet decides
# what a supplier's e-mail says between the lines (the replay of case:D01/D02 showed both kinds)
ROOM_SIGNALS = re.compile(
    r"can move further|come back to you on price|free capacity|step from your side|bridge the (?:remaining )?gap"
    r"|clarify this internally|happy to discuss|open to|we could consider|room to",
    re.I,
)
FIRM_SIGNALS = re.compile(
    r"cannot (?:reduce|lower|go) (?:the price )?(?:any )?further|all possible concessions"
    r"|no further (?:room|concession)|our (?:absolute )?limit|not able to move|this is our last"
    r"|must (?:\w+ )?(?:hold|maintain) our (?:current )?offer|does not allow us to reduce|unable to (?:reduce|improve)"
    r"|we maintain our (?:current )?offer",
    re.I,
)
APPROVAL_PENDING = re.compile(
    r"clarify (?:this |it )?internally|come back to you on (?:the )?price|my band|approv(?:e|al) (?:a|for) further|"
    r"check (?:the rest|internally)|discuss (?:this )?internally",
    re.I,

REANCHOR = 0.10  # an ungrounded floor the supplier undercuts at once: ask again this far under its price
BIG_STEP = 0.04  # a supplier move of 4 %+ in one round says it had room
UPPER_ROOM = 0.06  # the upper bound sits at least this far above our first ask
STOP_MARGIN = 0.01  # we take an offer within 1 % of where we expect the supplier to stop
MIN_STEP = 0.004  # every message moves at least 0.4 % of C: these bots punish a repeated offer
STOP_ROOM, UPPER_ROOM_SHARE = 0.05, 0.15  # the upper bound under a margin charge, as shares of the room
ANCHOR_SLACK = 0.25  # share of the room (quote to cost minimum) a deal on our deep first ask may cost
RELATIONSHIP_STEP = 0.25  # stabilise / secure_supply: our step as a share of the usual one
RELATIONSHIP_MIN_STEP = 0.05  # ... and at least this share of the room between its quote and our first ask
PATIENT_GAP = 0.01  # where we would meet its open offer early, we ask this far under it instead
PERSIST_STEP = 0.6  # `persistent`: our step as a share of the usual one ...
PERSIST_MIN = 0.006  # ... but never under 0.6 % of C: below 0.2 % the suppliers did not move at all (n 461)
MUST_CLAUSE = re.compile(
    r"must include an? [\w-]+ index clause|cannot offer a fixed price|requires? an? [\w-]+ "
    r"index clause",
    re.I,

FIGURES_ASKED = re.compile(
    r"Which figures is that based on|Please (?:send us|provide) the data|data that forms the basis", re.I
)
FIELD_WORDS = {

    "contract_months": "the contract length",
    "lead_time_days": "the lead time",
    "incoterm": "the delivery terms",
    "volume_per_year": "the volume",
    "index_clause": "an index clause",
    "effective_date": "the start date",
    "ppm_commitment": "the quality commitment",
    "chargeback_eur_per_complaint": "the chargeback",
    "tooling_eur": "tooling",
}
MAX_SPREAD = 0.08  # options of one message stay within 8 % of each other's price
EQUAL_C = 0.005  # ... and within 0.5 % of each other's C


def reply_signals(body: str) -> dict:
    """Room or firmness in the supplier's own words - a `final_offer` that asks for our step is no last word."""
    return {"room": bool(ROOM_SIGNALS.search(body or "")), "firm": bool(FIRM_SIGNALS.search(body or ""))}


EVIDENCE_FIRST = {  # profile trait / goal -> evidence kinds to put first
    "not_tracking_costs": ["index"],
    "open_book": ["should_cost"],
    "quality_first": ["quality", "scorecard"],
}


@dataclass
class Plan:
    supplier_id: str
    name: str
    policy: Policy
    profile: SupplierProfile
    open_c: float
    target_c: float
    floor_price: float | None
    full_cost: float | None
    gt: GroundTruth | None = None
    guess: dict | None = None  # a guessed supplier estimate (_fallback_full_cost): a price floor, not in C
    floor_countered: bool = False
    belief: FloorBelief | None = None  # where this supplier will stop with us - recomputed after every reply
    lower_c: float = -math.inf  # C at the supplier's estimated floor: take it at once
    upper_c: float = math.inf  # the most we accept when the deal is at risk - never said, never asked for
    evidence: list[Evidence] = field(default_factory=list)
    banned_kinds: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
    our_c: list[float] = field(default_factory=list)  # the C we asked for, per round
    last_claims: list[Evidence] = field(default_factory=list)
    seen_replies: int = 0
    stalls: int = 0
    probed_final: bool = False
    price_matched: bool = False
    requests: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)  # levers the supplier asked for in its e-mails
    last_keys: frozenset = frozenset()  # the structures and prices we sent last
    offered: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # structure -> the highest price we offered for it
    volume_proved: bool = False
    proposed: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # field -> values the supplier put on its own sheets
    text_price: float | None = None  # a lower price it wrote in the text but not on a sheet
    text_price_used: bool = False
    alternatives_taken: set = field(default_factory=set)
    counters: list = field(default_factory=list)  # facts from its own e-mails that answer it - spent first
    used_sentences: set = field(default_factory=set)
    lever_turn: bool = False  # this round our step goes into a structure we have not offered yet
    pressures: list = field(default_factory=list)  # cost drivers it says weigh on it
    request_counts: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # lever -> replies that asked for it
    reanchored: bool = False
    asked_breakdown: bool = False
    breakdown_read: bool = False
    stop_c: float = math.inf  # where the belief expects it to stop with us (C)
    figures_asked: bool = False  # its last e-mail asked for the figures behind our proposal
    figures_reply: bool = False
    answered_fixed: set = field(default_factory=set)  # fixed fields whose request we have answered
    spent_kinds: set = field(default_factory=set)  # argument kinds the arena called `duplicate` (fresh_args)

FLAGS: dict[str, str] = {
    "alt_structure": "its alternative's structure goes into our next menu; its price only on an end signal or at "
    "our stop estimate, never from a bidder behind the leader",
    "fresh_claims": "from round 2 up to 3 fresh arguments (complaints, should-cost too); 'Which figures?' answered "
    "with figures",
    "persistent": "longer and steadier: our floor estimate ends nothing until two rounds are left, our steps are "
    "60 % of the usual but never under 0.6 % of C",
    "answers": "plain answers: the volume we need, an opener that matches its move, a fixed field said once, a "
    "clause it must have kept, no 'pays early' that is not",
    "fresh_args": "never an argument the arena already counted (one per kind, index series, part); one held back from "
    "the first e-mail for a later round; a bundle's orders per part",
    "all_windows": "an index fall over the steepest window the arena accepts (<= 12 months, ending within the last "
    "12), not only one ending at the latest month; one per series",
    "news": "from round 2 one press report about the supplier's idle capacity (or the case's own news item), cited "
    "by ID next to the round's other arguments - the one checkable kind we never cited (docs/argument-audit.md)",
